text:
The meeting addressed Item 5, a recommendation to authorize the purchase of six vehicles. Council member Spencer raised concerns regarding the proposed purchase of three hybrid vehicles from Freeway Toyota in Hanford, California, for approximately $93,000. Spencer questioned why the city was not utilizing local Toyota dealerships, noting that the vehicles appeared to cost around $31,000 each.

Public Works Director Aaron Smith and Fleet Supervisor Heidrick clarified that the purchase is part of a state contract program, specifically C-Mass, administered by the Department of General Services (DGS) in Sacramento. They explained that all bidders for these state contracts are California-based dealerships. The city utilizes these state contracts rather than issuing local Requests for Proposals (RFPs) because participating dealerships handle high volumes of fleet vehicles, allowing them to secure significant price reductions from manufacturers.

Staff further explained that local dealerships typically prioritize selling to the general public, where profit margins are higher, and are often unwilling to sell fleet vehicles at prices significantly below retail. Consequently, leveraging state contracts or piggybacking on other entities’ purchases is the standard practice to ensure competitive pricing.

Following this explanation, Council member Spencer acknowledged the rationale. The council then proceeded to a vote. Council member Desert moved to authorize the purchase, and Council member Knox White seconded the motion. A roll call vote was initiated to finalize the decision.
